_: Alfie's brain in English (brain.py, answers.py): the sentences of his own commands in Home Assistant's sentence syntax ([optional], (this|that), {list}, <rule>), the lists and rules they use, and his replies. {name} and {area} are wildcards. Keys starting with _ are notes.

weather_forecast: (will it|is it going to|is it gonna) [be] {ask} [{span}] [<in_place>]
(will there|is there going to|is there gonna) be [any] {ask} [{span}] [<in_place>]
how is the weather [going to be] [looking] {span} [<in_place>]
sun: how (much|many hours of) (daylight|sunlight|sun) [is there|do we get|will we get|will there be] [{day}]
moon: <what_is> the (phase of the moon|moon's phase|moon phase|lunar phase) [tonight|now|today]
world_time: (what time is it|what's the time|what is the time|whats the time) [now|right now] in {place}
run: (turn on|switch on|start|run|launch|activate|trigger|begin|fire up|kick off|set off|do|play|start up|boot up|wake up|wake) [the|my|our] {name} [please]
help: what are you (able to do|good at|good for)
joke: (do you know|know|got|have you got|you got) any [good|funny|new] jokes
(i want|i'd like|i would like) [to hear] a joke
entity: how (much|many) {name} (is there|are there|do we have|is left|are left)

lists._: Each list: the words someone says -> what the answer code gets.

things._: What a word in 'how many lights are on' counts: domains, and device classes when given ("" is none). 'one' and 'many' are how a reply says it.

states._: How a state is said, by domain.device_class, then domain, then _any. Anything else: the state with underscores as spaces.

same_state: _ Groups of words that answer yes for each other: asked 'is the door open?', a door that is 'open' or 'on' is.

answers.not_now: {name} isn't {asked}, it's {state}, and has been for {ago}.
answers.since_long: {name} has been {state} for over a week.
answers.changed_long: {name} has been {state} for over a week.

outside._: Alfie's words about outside (outside.py): how conditions are said now, later, as a noun and as asked; which conditions are which kind; and his replies.

replies.lasts: The {asked} looks set to last as far as the forecast goes.
replies.none_ahead: No {asked} is forecast in the next {hours} hours.
replies.high_low: The high {span} is {hi}, and the low {lo}.
replies.temps_both: , a high of {hi} and a low of {lo}
replies.gear_cold_no: Probably not: it only gets down to {temp} {span}.
replies.gear_warm_no: Probably not: it only gets up to {temp} {span}.
replies.gear_sun_no: Probably not: the UV index stays at {uv} or below {span}.
replies.longer: That's {ago} more than the day before.
replies.shorter: That's {ago} less than the day before.
replies.moon_no: No, it's a {now}, {lit}% lit. The next {phase} is {when}.
replies.moon: It's a {now}, {lit}% lit. The next {phase} is {when}.

reckon._: Alfie's words for time, dates and numbers (reckon.py): named dates and their rules (MM-DD, MM/day/n with -1 the last, MM/day/<DD the last before that day, easter±N), place names for time zones, unit names, and his replies.

replies.year_left: It's day {n} of {total}, with {left} left in the year.
replies.leap_no: No, {year} isn't a leap year. The next one is {next}.

household._: People, media, calendar and lists (household.py). {name} a person, a player or a list; {what} a calendar event; {item} a list item.

replies.how_long_long: {name} has been {where} for over a week.
replies.no_album: I don't know the album of {what}.
replies.nothing_next: Nothing's coming up on your calendar.
replies.no_list: I can't find a list called {name}.

fun._: fun.py: chance, jokes, small talk and help. Jokes are "setup | punchline"; lines are picked at random; help's groups are said when any of their commands is on.

replies.too_many_dice: I can roll up to {most} dice, with up to a thousand sides each.
replies.no_jokes: I don't know any jokes yet.
replies.help_none: Not much right now: my own answers are all switched off.
replies.help_delegate: For anything else, I ask my bigger brain.

My name's {name}. I look after the house.

bored: Want a joke? Just ask me for one.

the weather, the sun and the moon
